A subject, followed along the whole path

One coffee, one chain

Codes and links that let any cup be followed back to its plot.

Start Before the first record

What it is

Roast keeps the records of a coffee from the plant to the cup. A grower writes down each day's picking, a processor each step from cherry to green, a roaster each roast, a brewer or taster each cup. Each record points to the one before it, so any cup can be followed back to the plot where it grew.

It runs in your phone's web browser. There is nothing to download from an app store, and no account is needed to start.

Seen fromRoast at a glance

What it is · See how one coffee's records link up

Every record sits somewhere on this path. You use only the part you need: a home brewer may only ever touch the last two, a grower who sells cherry only the first two.

  1. Plot
  2. Harvest
  3. Process run
  4. Green lot
  5. Roast
  6. Cup

Each arrow is a link the app keeps for you. A green lot made from a run knows its run; the run knows its harvests; the harvests know their plots. Nothing is typed twice.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceKilos carry forward

Why it matters

A buyer, a café or a visitor may ask where a coffee came from and how it was made. When each record points to the one before, the answer is already there.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceRecords you can trust

Step 8 · Add something new from anywhere

The bar at the bottom stays in reach of your thumb. New adds a harvest, process run, reading, green lot, roast, brew or cup, colour reading or plot. Find opens Find. Home goes home. Scan reads a KoffyKraft QR with the camera, or from a saved photo or screenshot.

Seen fromYour first day, step 8Finding your way

Step 9 · Find a plot, lot or code

Type in the Find box on Home or Now, or tap Find. Type part of a name or a code. Your records come first, each with its kind on the right. Tap one to open it. Under the results: Searched on this phone. Works with no signal.

Seen fromYour first day, step 9Finding your way

Why it matters

Codes and names are how records find each other. When a lot comes up after three letters, a buyer's question gets answered standing in the store room.

Seen fromYour first day

Harvest The day's picking

What it is

A harvest says what was picked, where and when. Later a process run takes its cherry from one or more harvests, and the green lot it makes points back through them to the plots. You need at least one plot first; if you have none yet, save the harvest now and tick its plots later.

Seen fromLogging a harvest

Step 2

Tap + Harvest. The Harvest code and Date are filled in. The code is made from the date: H, then year, month and day, then a number for the day (H261102-1 is the first harvest on 2 November 2026).

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 2

Step 3 · Say which plots were picked

Change the Date if you picked on another day (Start time and End time are optional). Under Plots picked, tick each plot. Choose the Picking (Selective, Strip, Gleaning or Mixed) and the number of Pickers.

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 3

Process run Cherry to green

What it is

A run follows one batch through floating, pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, resting and hulling. It takes its cherry from your harvests, so it already knows the plots, and the green lot made at the end takes its weight from the run.

Seen fromProcess runsKilos carry forward

Step 1 · Start a processing run

Open Origin, the Process tab, and tap + Process. The Process code is made from the date (P, then year, month and day).

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromProcess runs, step 1

Step 3 · Take the cherry from my harvests

Under Source harvests, tick the harvests in this batch; each shows its code, date and kilos. Cherry in adds up. For cherry not logged as a harvest, leave them unticked and type the kilos in Cherry in (if not from harvests). Check Started.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 3Kilos carry forward

Step 10

The run's page shows the chain from plot to harvest to this run, and Share to a space, Image or PDF and Passport and QR.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 10

Green lot What goes to the roaster

What it is

A green lot is what goes to the roaster. Your own coffee points back to its run, and through it to the harvests and plots. Bought coffee keeps its origin as the seller states it. Every roast later picks a green lot as its source, and the stock goes down by itself.

Seen fromGreen lotsKilos carry forward

Step 1 · Make a green lot from my run

Open Origin, the Green tab, and tap + Green lot. The Green lot code is made from the date (G, then year, month and day). Give it a Name people will recognise.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 1

Step 2

Under From process, pick the run. Its chain shows, and a message: Green weight filled from the run, with the kilos from the run's last Out kg. Change it if the scale says otherwise.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 2Kilos carry forward

Step 5

Tap Save. The lot's page shows its chain back to plot, harvest and run, how much is left, and This lot, Quality and stock, EUDR, Sack labels and For a buyer.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 5

Step 6 · Record coffee I bought in

For bought coffee, leave From process empty and fill Bought coffee: origin as the seller states it: Farm or washing station, Producer, Region, Country, Variety, Process, Altitude, m, Harvest, Bought from, Lot or auction number, Invoice date. Use the words on the seller's papers.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 6

Watch out

A lot with no process and nothing under Bought from still saves, with a message: Not linked to a process. Pick its process, or fill Bought from to mark it bought in. Without one of the two, nobody can tell where it came from.

Seen fromGreen lotsRecords you can trust

Step 9 · Print sack labels

Tap Sack labels: one 100 by 50 mm label per bag, with a QR, the lot code, name and estate, process, moisture, date and Bag 1 of 1. Tap Print at the top. The QR opens this lot in the app; once the lot has a passport, it opens the passport, which anyone can check.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 9

Tip

If the labels do not open, the phone may be blocking pop-ups for the app. Allow them and tap Sack labels again.

Seen fromGreen lots
